correctness.rationale: For every finite connected simple triangle-free H, the vertex-incidence model makes each even/odd Čech generator explicit by Adams–Shukla–Singh Lemma 2.2. The proof partitions extra faces into unique markers and removes them by descending-cardinality codimension-one free pairs, first from scale three to the cross-edge complex and then to scale two. Two further exact collapses produce a graph with original-vertex star trees and reversal edges, homotopy equivalent to H. The injection and direct-sum decomposition of local complete-graph cycle lattices gives the integral kernel and surjectivity. All degree-one and zero-cycle boundaries are covered. A standalone standard-library program checked every individual relative collapse in 38 finite triangle-free graphs and computed the C3 mod-two sharpness witness; experiments corroborate but do not replace the universal proof.

value.rationale: The result gives an explicit relative elementary collapse and exact integral persistence-kernel classification across a natural infinite graph family with arbitrary degrees and cycle rank. For degrees at least three the truncated graph contains 3-cycles so the generic r<girth/2 nerve reconstruction theorem cannot certify persistence at r=3. The proof separates local clique cycles dying at scale two from global cycles persisting to scale three, with a sharp triangle-base counterexample. This is structural inclusion-level information, not a routine table recomputation.
